title: Computer Problem Delays About 1,000 Delta Flights
summary: Sunday was a hard travel day for Delta passengers. A problem with a computer system delayed well over half of Delta's flights on Sunday afternoon, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The broken system works out how heavy a plane is. That number matters: a plane must not be too heavy to fly, and crews use the weight to keep the flight safe. While the system was down, Delta's teams did the work by hand to get planes off the ground. Hours later, Delta said the system was working again, but flights were still not back to normal. By Sunday afternoon, about 1,000 Delta flights were delayed. The flight-tracking website FlightAware said that was 67 percent of the airline's flights. Earlier on Sunday, the Federal Aviation Administration stopped some flights heading into Atlanta's airport for an hour. Atlanta is Delta's home base and one of the busiest airports in the world. Delta said sorry and promised new flights for customers, plus meals and hotel rooms where needed, and refunds if a flight was canceled. About 2 percent of flights were canceled.
why_it_matters: If you fly to visit family for Thanksgiving, a computer problem like this can mean long waits at the airport or a changed flight.

background_read: Before a plane takes off, the airline has to know how heavy it is, because a plane that is too heavy cannot fly safely.
Delta uses a computer system to work out that weight, but the system broke down on Sunday.
With the system down, workers had to do the work by hand, which slowed everything down and delayed about 1,000 flights.
